alt: Wide view of Lake Khövsgöl and the forested hills of its western shore in summer.
caption: Lake Khövsgöl photographed in June, when it is open water. The same lake is frozen to more than a metre in March and is the stage for the winter days at Khatgal; this shows the shoreline and taiga hills the ice road follows.

alt: Aerial view of a crowd and parked vehicles on the snow-covered ice of Lake Khövsgöl during the Ice Festival.
caption: An aerial view of the Ice Festival on the frozen lake near Khatgal, with spectators ringed around the competition area and vehicles parked directly on the ice. Dates are announced each year, usually in early March, so the trip is built to move with them.

alt: Aerial view of the Ice Festival gathering around a cleared ice arena with gers and tents beside it.
caption: The festival arena from above: a cleared sheet of ice surrounded by crowds, gers and tents. It is a community gathering first and a visitor event second, which is why we plan to arrive a day early and stay with a Khatgal host family.

location: Khongoryn Els, Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park
alt: Long ridge of the Khongoryn Els sand dunes under a clear sky.
caption: The Khongoryn Els dunes, the 'singing sands' of the southern Gobi, photographed in July. In winter they carry a light dusting of snow and the air is dry and still; the ridge is a short, cold walk from the herder family ger we use as a base.

location: Khongoryn Els, Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park
alt: Bactrian camels standing in front of the Khongoryn Els dunes.
caption: Bactrian camels grazing at the foot of Khongoryn Els (summer photograph). Herder families here keep the two-humped camels year-round, and a short ride with the host family is the usual way to cross to the dune base in winter.

location: Yolyn Am, Gobi Gurvansaikhan National Park
alt: Narrow rocky gorge of Yolyn Am in the Gobi Altai.
caption: The Yolyn Am gorge in the Gobi Altai (summer photograph). The valley floor holds ice into early summer and in February-March it is a frozen walkway between the cliffs, a short drive from Dalanzadgad.

alt: Red sandstone cliffs of Bayanzag rising from the Gobi plain.
caption: The Flaming Cliffs at Bayanzag, where the first dinosaur eggs were found in the 1920s. Photographed in August; in March the saxaul forest below is bare and the cliffs sit under a hard blue sky.

alt: A harem group of Przewalski's horses (takhi) on the steppe of Hustai National Park.
caption: Takhi, Przewalski's horses, reintroduced to Hustai from zoo stock in the 1990s (summer photograph). The park is about two hours from Ulaanbaatar and visits are ranger-guided; winter visibility of herds is not guaranteed.

alt: Temple buildings and courtyard of Gandantegchinlen Monastery photographed in late November.
caption: Gandan, the main working Buddhist monastery in Ulaanbaatar, photographed on 30 November. It is the first cultural stop of the trip and a calm place to acclimatise to the cold.

commonsFile: File:Meat from a freshly butchered cow being frozen on the roofs of the gers (Mongolia 2010 208).jpg
alt: Winter slaughtered beef freezing on top of gers in a Mongolian settlement.
caption: Winter butchering: meat is frozen on the ger roofs and kept for months, which is what fills the table at Tsagaan Sar and in homestays. Photographed in late November; the same practice runs through February.

alt: Festive Tsagaan Sar table with stacked biscuits, dumplings and dairy dishes.
caption: A Tsagaan Sar table with the traditional stacked bread tier and buuz dumplings. Tsagaan Sar 2027 begins around 7 February; our March window misses it, but this is the food a host family serves for any big winter meal.

alt: Rock formations and valley of Gorkhi-Terelj National Park.
caption: The granite valleys of Gorkhi-Terelj, an hour and a half from Ulaanbaatar. Photographed in spring; in winter this is the final ger night and a walk to Turtle Rock in deep snow.
